decision.account: All seven corpus papers now have ready_to_synthesize answers (Du 2023, Lorenz 2011, Choi 2025, Dung 1995, Shapiro 2011, Smit 2023, Zhang 2025); the wave-1 blocked answers are superseded by their r2 counterparts. The five open raised questions (rz1, rz2, rq1, rq-choi-1, rq-shapiro-merge) are identification gaps the corpus cannot settle, and both synthesis questions' rationales direct that they be carried into the D6 limits and D7 experiment design rather than investigated further. The highest-information-value bounded action is therefore the integrative synthesis that converts the seven answers into the mechanistic thesis (D2), causal model (D3), reconciliation (D4), discriminating predictions (D5), limits (D6), experiment skeleton (D7), and warranted conclusion (D8). question:work:003-synthesis and question:work:004-synthesis draw on the identical evidence base and overlap in content, so one synthesis action covering both is bounded and avoids a redundant step; nothing about this synthesis requires a peer result, since it only integrates already-named answers.

action.acceptance_condition: The synthesis answer contains: (1) a single-sentence mechanistic thesis with explicit scope conditions naming when staged retrieval-mediated Q/A wins or loses at matched compute; (2) a causal model listing the six nodes, their directed edges, sign conditions, and per-edge epistemic status; (3) a reconciliation mapping each of the seven papers to model variables with workspace file paths and explicit ===== PDF PAGE N ===== markers inherited from the source answers, distinguishing reported findings, cross-paper inference, and the note's new hypothesis; (4) at least four discriminating predictions, each tagged with the alternative (compute-only, diversity-only, deliberation-only) it excludes; (5) a limits section naming rz1, rz2, rq1, rq-choi-1, and rq-shapiro-merge and stating why existing evidence cannot settle them; (6) an experiment skeleton covering units, task strata, conditions, randomization, intervention fidelity, primary and secondary estimands, outcome measures, power-analysis inputs, exclusion rules, multiple-testing control, and stopping/failure criteria; (7) a closing paragraph with the strongest warranted conclusion, material unresolved questions, and the single observation most likely to falsify the thesis.
action.conflict_policy: Reconcile by mechanism and moderators, never by preferred outcome: attribute Du's positives to unmatched-compute, weakest-baseline comparisons (per Zhang's page-marked reconciliation claim), Smit's nulls/sign flips to dataset-specific optimal agreement intensity, and Zhang's negatives to matched-call budgets and single-knowledge-point benchmark topology, while treating heterogeneity's debate-specific value (rz1) and knowledge-combination topology (rz2) as genuinely non-identified. Every conflicting pair must be explained by an explicit moderator variable in the causal model, and each claim must be labeled reported finding, cross-paper inference, or new hypothesis.
action.objective: Integrate the seven corpus answers into the note's core: (a) one original mechanistic thesis stating when staged retrieval-mediated Q/A beats both independent sampling with final aggregation and an open shared transcript under matched inference compute; (b) an explicit causal model over initial error correlation, evidence diversity, social influence/conformity, retrieval selectivity, synthesis competence, and task topology, with each edge labeled corpus-evidenced, cross-paper inference, or non-identified; (c) a reconciliation, without discarding any finding, of Du's positives, Smit's hyperparameter/dataset-contingent nulls and agreement-intensity sign flips, and Zhang's matched-compute SC dominance plus heterogeneity gains, using Lorenz and Choi for the social-influence pathway and Dung and Shapiro for the truth-neutral adjudication/merge stage; (d) at least four directional or interaction predictions, each tagged with the alternative it excludes (compute-only, diversity-only, deliberation-only); (e) a limits section mapping rz1, rz2, rq1, rq-choi-1, and rq-shapiro-merge to the specific causal edges they leave non-identified; (f) a preregisterable matched-compute experiment skeleton (units, strata, conditions, randomization, fidelity, estimands, power inputs, exclusion rules, multiple-testing control, stopping/failure criteria) instantiating rz1 and rz2; (g) the strongest warranted conclusion and the single most falsifying observation.
action.rationale: The raw materials exist as named answers with page-marked citations, and the evidence base is contradictory exactly as the dossier intends: Du shows debate > majority but never matches compute; Zhang replicates MAD > single-agent yet shows the ordering collapses against CoT/SC at matched ~6-call budgets and that heterogeneity helps every framework; Smit shows dataset- and hyperparameter-contingent effects with sign flips; Lorenz and Choi bracket the conformity pathway from bare-answer and rationale-mediated sides; Dung and Shapiro show adjudication and merging are truth-neutral and that stochastic LLM synthesis violates CRDT convergence conditions. Only integration can convert this into the thesis, model, predictions, limits, and experiment the demands require; further corpus investigation cannot close the raised gaps.
